answer: In an agent marketplace buying tundra surveys, canyon maps, and basalt classifications, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before submitting at most one bid per hour. Opening more identities therefore requires more locked capital: 1,000 fake agents tie up $100,000 for a month. The bond does not prove identities are unique; it makes multiplying them costly and limits how cheaply an attacker can flood the market with bids.
